Stega in the yajurveda Saṃhitās seems to denote a species of ‘worm.’ The word occurs in the Rigveda also, where its sense is unknown, but may possibly be ‘ploughshare.’
Foot notes taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 7, 11, 1; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxv. 1.
x. 31, 9 = Av. xviii. 1, 39. Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 98.
Weber, Proceedings of the Berlin Academy, 1895, 833. Cf. Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 824.

Stena is a common word for ‘thief’ from the Rigveda onwards. See taskara.
Foot notes ii. 23, 16; 28, 10; 42, 3, etc.
Av. iv. 3, 4, 5; 36, 7; xix. 47, 6; aitareya brāhmaṇa, v. 30, 11, etc.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 178 et seq.

Steya denotes ‘theft’ in the Atharvaveda and later. Cf. dharma.
Foot notes xi. 8, 20; xiv. 1, 57.
nirukta, vi. 27; kauṣītaki upaniṣad, iii. 1. Cf. steya-kṛt, ‘thief,’ in Rv. vii. 104, 10.
